compute: CPU-only, NumPy 2.5.3, Python 3.13. No GPU. Estimates are hypotheses, not measured GPU time.
hardware_scope: Local Windows x86-64 CPU; NOT the A100-PCIE-40GB MX target. Ratios are hardware-independent structure counts; GPU latencies not measured.

synthetic_cost_model.note: Reproduced faithfully from packaged cpu_oracle.py (logical content byte-identical to packaged out/s42, out/s123).
synthetic_cost_model.g2_synthetic_read: active_hit/tile_bbox_candidate at tile32 = 0.21-0.24 (seed42) and 0.24 (seed123). Borderline vs gate <=0.20. stream_candidates not directly comparable (kit counts conservative padded candidates, not exact-support hits). Synthetic tiny-workload; NOT scene evidence.

real_cohort_cost_model.method: Per-camera over SPD+opacity>=cutoff AND actually-intersected gaussians. Candidate baselines: (a) conservative per-Gaussian tile footprint from 3-sigma screen radius (gsplat/FastGS math, tiles/gaussian); (b) row-span conservative pixel candidates from the kit's xy_bounds. Intersection pairs from the kernel's own gaussian_ids. H,W=1600x1066, tile=16.

G2.preregistered: CONTINUE requires (a) active_hit/tile_bbox_candidate <=0.20 AND (b) stream_candidate/tile_bbox_candidate <=0.35 on >=2/3 scenes (=> >=5x exact-hit arithmetic gap and >=~2.86x conservative-stream candidate reduction).
G2.real_data_result: FAIL. (a) real kernel intersections are ~2% of the conservative footprint, i.e. the EXISTING renderer already achieves >>5x over its own conservative footprint via exact ellipse + opacity culling; the opportunity is already captured by the baseline, not by a new structure. (b) The proposed row-span candidate stream is ~6.8x DENSER than the conservative footprint pixel count it would replace (median rowspan/footprint = 6.79, per-gaussian footprint tiles median ~59 vs row-span candidates ~183-1120/g). The 'compressed stream' is larger, not smaller, than the structure it targets.
G2.synthetic_note: tile32 active/bbox ~0.21-0.24 borderline; but synthetic tiny-workload is not scene evidence and the kit's own stream_candidate metric is padded-conservative, not exact-support.

G4.preregistered: Same-hardware measured f of affected complete training time; S_max = 1/(1-f); 3x requires f>=2/3. Count projection/optimizer/loss/densification separately.
G4.real_data_result: BLOCKED (not measured). No GPU authorized; no same-hardware Faster-GS fused f captured. On REAL room data the rasterizer binning/intersection build already performs exact opacity+ellipse culling (real_intersect/footprint ~0.02), so the residual addressable fraction of *binning/intersection build* is small AND already occupied by the existing culling. Amdahl ceiling on the remaining gap is far below the f>=2/3 needed for 3x.

G5.preregistered: Model worst-case memory/bytes of materializing sparse list incl sort+prefix offsets+fwd/bwd reuse vs exact tile32 + AccuTile and gsplat index extraction; optimistic model must allow >=1.30x full-step with nonnegative extra memory.
G5.real_data_result: FAIL (headroom negative). The proposed per-row span materialization costs ~6.8x the candidate bytes of the per-tile footprint it replaces (row_span_candidates vs footprint_tile_pixels), plus it must ADD a separate CSR/segment materialization on top of gsplat's already-shipped packed per-tile index (which #3 of prior art already reuses in both passes). Net: more global bytes and more build traffic than the current renderer, not less. Optimistic upper bound is <1.0x on the intersection stage and cannot reach the >=1.30x full-step requirement with nonnegative memory budget.

headroom_summary: On real room-scene data the strongest existing renderer (FastGS/gsplat-class) already culls to ~2% of its conservative footprint via exact ellipse + opacity tests. The proposed compressed per-row support stream is ~6.8x DENSER than the structure it would replace and adds a materialization pass on top of an already-shipped packed/sparse index. Theoretical headroom is negative for the intersection/binning stage; no path to the preregistered >=1.30x full-step or 3x E2E.
